title: refactor(agents): unify env
body:
Unify environment variables in agents. Now, all* of the agents are unified to use env vars `LLM_API_KEY`, `LLM_API_BASE` and `LLM_MODEL`, assuming an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

This could eventually help us implement our own OpenAI-compatible endpoint proxy, but for now it at least unifies most of the agents under a single interface.

Yeah, this potentially limits compatibility with extra features of some providers. But it seems like a good tradeoff at this point.

~*`gpt-researcher` uses an embedding endpoint which is not available on Groq, so I left it at the current state (Ollama only) for the time being.~
author: JanPokorny

comments.body:
This collides with our current env management, are we sure we want to go this way now?

`beeai env add API_KEY=...` will set the api key globally for all providers after this PR because they'll use the same env name.

There might be a use-case where I want `openai` for one agent but grok for another one for example, the current approach with `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `GROK_API_KEY` would allow it

We'd need to re-introduce per-provider configuration to make this sufficiently configurable

@jezekra1 My take is:
- it was partially like that already (eg. `API_BASE` used by several agents)
- for the demo we need lowest friction possible => we can't really make it zero-config but this is the fewest config manageable
- going forward we may want to either:
	- provide an in-platform OpenAI-compatible API proxy, which could allow LLM routing on the platform level (and do fancy stuff like actually count token usage per agent)
	- or at least allow for per-agent (/ per-provider?) config
	- or at the very least allow for something like `beeai env add --only=aider-agent API_KEY=...`
I'd personally prefer to prefix the envs with `BEEAI_`
Accidentally merged without creating a PR, sorry for that.

title: Demonstrate example use case
body:
Let's demonstrate capabilities of the platform with following use case:

We can leverage existing functionality of the platform to combine`gpt-researcher` and `aider` to perform deep research of something that is numericaly heavy.

The output of the research can then be fed to `aider` to create a webpage that would allow visualising those data in form of simple charts.

We should leverage sequential composition agent to achieve the result.

As @JanPokorny correctly pointed out - we can't just easily use composition agent because we need to separate data from  prompt. Basically the composition is as follows:

1. Prompt gpt-researcher with "Perform a deep research on given topic resulting numerical heavy data"
2. The result is a document (data) that can then be fed to aider but additional prompt has to be provided "Create a nextjs app that will visualize given data using D3 library"
3. Artefact is generated that user can start

Realistically we need to create new  "prompt sequential flow" agent that would allow this prompted approach. 


Example prompts:

- I want to understand the tradeoffs of buying a new vs used car. Or, electric vs hybrid, vs gas car. Make a webpage or interactive chart that allows me to select various makes and models of cars and see their change in value over time.
- Research past 10 years of crypto market and provide information about most valuable crypto currencies providing the market capitalization and its value over time. Plot the result to charts that i can dynamically filter by years.

title: Orchestration - sequential flows
body:
Let's create a "composition" agent that takes as an input:
```
agents: string[]
prompt: string
```

The agent would chain the agents in a sequence flow, just handing over the output -> input.

The implementation of the agent chaining should be ideally done through Workflows. Other things to figure out:
- Add an extra field `type: "agent" | "composition" that the UI and CLI can use to treat these agents as compositions
- Figure out some simple standard on how notifications from these agents can be propagated back to the collar

title: Agent Library Registration
body:
Yet to be defined.

We need support for:

- Add Github repo
- Add local files
- Add remote provider
author: tomkis

comments.body: @tomkis can you give an example of how to add a remote provider? would that be a direct link to the agent code? I'm trying to understand if we add 2 entry points (GitHub / provider) or if we fork the UX after a single CTA

There are basically three ways how one can import agent library.

1. Provide a link to github repo, the app will then scrape down all the content and imports
2. Provide a link to local file system where agent library is implemented
3. Remote URL to running provider (agent library)

Keep in mind, agent library registration does make sense only in local experience as hosted experience will be managed by us (through code).

Agent library may contain more than one agent to be imported and they are all imported transactionally (all or none). There can be imported unlimited libraries at once.

User should have an option to unregister whole library (transactionally) by simply removing the link from the app.
